author: krealalejo
body:
Started as an analysis of what stood between the app and feeling smooth. Five areas came out of it; all five are here, across 41 commits.

## Data loss (the reason this branch exists)

Nine store actions mutated local state and never called the API, so the changes vanished on reload. Every endpoint already existed — the store just wasn't calling them.

| Action | Now calls |
|---|---|
| `toggleShop`, `setShopQty`, `setShopPrice` | `PATCH /api/shopping` |
| `addManualShop` | `POST /api/shopping` |
| `removeShop` | `DELETE /api/shopping` |
| `deleteInv` | `DELETE /api/inventory` + linked shopping rows |
| `invite` | `POST /api/members` |
| `revoke`, `removeMember` | `DELETE /api/members` |

Each updates optimistically and rolls back on failure, matching the store's existing pattern.

Related fixes:

- **Checkout never persisted restocks.** `qty = optimal` was set in memory only, so after a reload the item was low again and auto-restock re-added it — repeating on every shop.
- **Temp-id race.** Rows inserted optimistically carried a `temp_` id until their POST returned; touching one in that window sent that id to the server and 404'd. Calls now park on the in-flight create. Temp ids also moved to `crypto.getRandomValues` — the old `Date.now()` ids collided on same-millisecond taps.
- **Invites didn't survive reload.** `members.post` wrote a `PendingInvite` but `members.get` only read `User`. The list now merges both, and `members.delete` falls back to `PendingInvite`.
- The "Invitation sent" toast fired unconditionally; it now waits for the POST.

## Sessions expiring every hour

Access tokens last 1h, refresh tokens 30d, and `/api/auth/refresh` was implemented and tested — with zero callers. A 401 sent users straight to `/login`.

New `api()` wrapper refreshes once and retries. `refreshSession()` dedupes concurrent client refreshes; on SSR it proxies `Set-Cookie` to the browser *and* rewrites the request cookie, so the rest of that render uses the new token instead of re-401ing.

## Two id-vs-name bugs

`assignee` holds a user id but was compared against `currentUser`, which holds a display name. The dashboard "Mine" filter was always empty, and on the household page it hid the "You" tag and both the remove and leave buttons.

## Perceived speed

- The layout awaited `useBootstrap()` at the top level, so Suspense held the whole app behind seven requests. Shell paints immediately now, data fills in.
- The auth middleware hit `/api/auth/me` on every route change even though bootstrap already had the user.
- Skeletons on all six data pages — load-bearing, not decoration: without them the faster boot flashes each page's empty state before data lands.
- The quantity stepper fired one PATCH per tap. It now keeps its own display value and debounces the emit, so the number still moves instantly while five taps send one request.

## i18n, a11y, feedback

- The `login.*` and `profile.*` keys existed in all three locales and nothing referenced them. Wired up, plus ~90 new keys.
- Every store toast was hardcoded English, so switching language left all feedback untranslated.
- New locale-parity test checks es/ca against en for missing keys, extra keys, placeholder drift and lost plural forms. It caught a real English bug: `history.purchasesCount` rendered "1 trips".
- `prefers-reduced-motion` was declared in CSS but GSAP writes inline styles the media query can't reach, so every animation still played in full.
- Icon-only controls labelled; toasts announced via a polite live region; sidebar profile card given real button semantics.
- Checkout and add-item buttons show pending state.
- Accent colour now previews live and reverts on dismiss (was `TODO.md`: "switching color in profile is not working").

## Verification

436 tests pass, production build clean, dev server boots with no warnings. Coverage 93.7% statements / 87.9% branches, above the 80% thresholds.

## Not included

- `app/pages/privacy.vue` is still English-only. It's a legal document — machine-translating it would make the policy say subtly different things per language, which is a call for a human to make.
- `TODO.md` still lists the profile avatar transition and `/privacy` being unreachable while logged in.

## Note on history

Commits are granular by design. A few early ones land wrapper plumbing before the test suites are updated, so `git bisect` across that span isn't clean, though each commit is coherent on its own.

author: marcus-girolneto
body:
Develop counterpart of #1573.

## Summary

Aligns the data application acceptance path with the validation node-shared already performs immediately before acceptance, so the two layers reach the same verdict on the same transactions.

Every behaviour change is routed through `FieldsAddedOrdinals` entries. Snapshots signed below the activation ordinal continue to replay under the rules they were produced with, so rejoin, download and consensus validation recreate them unchanged, and a rolling upgrade does not split consensus.

## Why new config keys rather than `fee-transaction-security`

`fee-transaction-security` is already open on integrationnet at `5880000`. Widening what that gate controls would change how signed history between `5880000` and now replays on that network, which is exactly the failure the gate exists to prevent. Two new entries are used instead:

- `fixing-data-application-fee-validation`
- `fixing-allow-spend-destination-credit`

## Gate inputs

Both gates read an ordinal carried by the history being replayed, not the node's live view of the global chain:

- currency side: the previous snapshot's `globalSyncView` ordinal, already threaded as `parentGlobalSnapshotOrdinal`
- global side: the ordinal of the snapshot being built

A node replaying an old ordinal therefore evaluates the gate exactly as the node that produced it did.

## Notable

`validateFeeTxs` in `BalanceOpsManager` is gated as well. Below activation it keeps raising. The drop changes which artifact acceptance produces from the same events, and below activation the data application layer is on its legacy validator, which checks neither `source != destination` nor signature exclusivity, so such a transaction still reaches acceptance. A patched node dropping it while an unpatched node raises would split the rollout window.

## Activation

Mainnet activates at global ordinal **6818000**, at/after. `testnet` and `integrationnet` are placeholders (`9999999`) and must be pinned before those networks upgrade. `dev` is `0`, so a fresh network runs the current rules from genesis.

Roll the binary out to every Currency L1 and ML0 node before the activation ordinal is reached.

## Verification

- `compile` and `Test/compile` clean across all modules (Java 21).
- 26 tests pass in the touched suites: `FeeTransactionValidatorSuite`, `AllowSpendBlockAcceptanceLogicSuite`, and the node-shared snapshot manager suites.
- `scalafmtAll` clean.

## Not covered

The activation gates themselves have no unit test - reaching them needs a stubbed `BaseDataApplicationL0Service`, `L0NodeContext` and `CalculatedStateLocalFileSystemStorage`.

author: weirdapps
body:
## The bug

`_extract_one_attachment` read `response.content[0].text`. With extended thinking the model leads the content list with a `ThinkingBlock`, which exposes `.thinking` and no `.text`, so every such response died with:

```
AttributeError: 'ThinkingBlock' object has no attribute 'text'
```

**132 rows** in `attachment_content.llm_error` carry exactly that string, most recent `2026-08-25T02:15:50`, with **10,107 rows** stuck at `llm_status='pending'` behind it.

## The fix

The repo already had `_response_text`, which walks the blocks and returns the first one carrying text. The attachment, calendar and teams paths simply were not using it. They are now, so there is a single reader of a Claude response and the same bug cannot reappear in a fourth place.

Two shapes genuinely have no text: a thinking-only response truncated at `max_tokens`, and an empty content list. Both used to raise a bare "contained no text block" that said nothing about why. The message now carries `stop_reason` and the block type names, so the persisted `llm_error` is diagnosable on its own, which is the treatment `image_vision` already had.

Also wires the `sb-brain-freshness` Healthchecks ping into `health_check.py`'s existing OK/WARN/STALE status. That check had existed since 2026-08-09 with one ping in its life, because no code anywhere pinged it.

## Deliberately not changed

`calendar_extractor` sits at `max_tokens=1024` while every other site uses 8192 or 2048, which is a plausible latent instance of the same family. Measured before touching it: **zero** no-text failures in any log across 872 events. Left alone, and the improved error message makes it a one-line fix if it ever does bite.

## Tests

179 pass. Five fail identically on `master` and on this branch, all from `policy_bridge.py:49` referencing `anthropic.OverloadedError`, absent from the Mac venv's SDK 0.96.0. The VPS runs 0.122.0 where it exists, and zero rows in the production DB carry that error, so it is local venv drift and not a defect in this change.

## After merge

The 10,107 pending rows need a re-run to drain.

author: thomasvan
body:
## Why

- **Use case:** Running OpenDesign from source with a script-injecting browser
  extension installed (observed: a "popups" helper, extension id
  `lgblnfidahcdcjddiepkckcfdhpknnjh`, file `content/popups-script.js`) produces
  a React hydration-mismatch console error on every page load, pointed at
  `app/layout.tsx`.
- **Pain:** The error is console noise, but it reads like an app bug to
  developers and gets copy-pasted into issue reports. The extension rewrites
  the theme-init `<script>` node before React hydrates — it injects its own
  `src` attribute and empties `__html` — which is exactly React's documented
  "a browser extension … messes with the HTML before React loaded" case.
  Suppressing hydration checks on that node removes the noise without touching
  product behavior. There is no issue opened for this; it is a small hygiene
  fix.

## What users will see

Nothing visible changes — the app looks and behaves the same. Developers who
run script-injecting extensions no longer see a spurious
"A tree hydrated but some attributes of the server rendered HTML didn't match"
console error on every load.

## Surface area

- [x] **None** — internal refactor: adds `suppressHydrationWarning` to the
  theme-init `<script>` in the root layout, consistent with the existing
  `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>`/`<body>`. No new/removed UI, no
  dependency, API, contract, CLI flag, env var, i18n key, or default-behavior
  change.

## Screenshots

N/A — no UI surface checked.

## Bug fix verification

- Test path: intentionally none.
- Red on `main` / green on this branch: not applicable — a unit test cannot
  cheaply reproduce the failure: it requires a browser extension to rewrite
  the SSR-ed DOM before React hydrates. A Playwright spec could approximate
  the tampering via `addInitScript` DOM surgery, but this fix is a
  console-noise suppression with no functional surface, so extending that
  suite was judged disproportionate for this patch.
- Verified instead: with the extension active the console error reproduces on
  `main`; after the patch the page still serves HTTP 200 with the theme-init
  script intact, `pnpm --filter @open-design/web typecheck` passes, and the
  mismatch error no longer appears.

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter @open-design/web typecheck` ✅
- Manual: page loads (HTTP 200) with the theme script intact; mismatch error
  gone with the reported extension active.

author: agustin-y2k
body:
Dos arreglos que salieron de usar el sistema en computadora.

**Las casillas de "mantener la sesión iniciada" ahora son dos, una por camino de ingreso.** Había una sola, arriba del botón de "Iniciar sesión", y el de Google queda abajo del separador: mirando la pantalla no había forma de saber si valía también para ese camino. Valía, pero eso solo lo sabía el código.

Son excluyentes —marcar una desmarca la otra— y la exclusión no la hace ningún código: el campo pasó de booleano a `"ninguna" | "password" | "google"` y las dos casillas leen y escriben ese mismo valor, así que no hay dos estados que puedan quedar desincronizados.

El precio queda testeado y no librado al azar: la casilla vale para el botón que tiene al lado, así que quien marque la de contraseña y termine entrando con Google recibe la sesión corta. **RF-01.13 cambió de comportamiento** y por eso es un minor y no un patch.

**Un nombre largo ya no rompe la barra de navegación.** El bloque del nombre no tenía tope y el `nav` de al lado es quien tiene `flex-1`, así que crecía a costa de los enlaces: el menú de todos quedaba detrás de una barra de desplazamiento horizontal para mostrar entero el apellido de uno. Medido a 1536px, en la barra de un Admin el nombre entra en 80px y ni "Ada Lovelace" mide tan poco, así que el Admin pasa a ver solo el redondel con sus iniciales —como ya veía entre 1024 y 1535px— y el docente lo conserva con tope de 256px. De paso, la barra horizontal aparece a partir de 1100px y no de 1024, donde entraba apretada y partía "Horario Admins" en dos renglones.

Documentación al día: RF-01.13, seguridad, la guía de docentes con la captura del ingreso regenerada, y las portadas de las dos guías en «versión 1.16».

Sin cambios de esquema ni de `.env`.

- `/dashboard/thalassemia/patients/:id` — patient detail with 10 tabs:
  1. **Checklist** — auto-computed matrix (investigations × timepoints) with done / overdue flags and one-click "Enter now" shortcuts
  2. Demographics
  3. Labs (21 fields — MMPs, ferritin, LPI, NT-proBNP, LFTs, endocrine, CRP)
  4. ECG (10 fields)
  5. Echo (24 fields, grouped by Systolic / LV Dimensions / Volumes / LA / Diastology / RV)
  6. T2* MRI (4 fields)
  7. PSG (16 fields — full AHI panel, OSA severity)
  8. SCG (8 fields — EF, CO, SV, AI confidence)
  9. Transfusions (log linked to ad-hoc ECG)
  10. Adverse Events (severity, relatedness, serious flag, MREC reporting)
- `/dashboard/thalassemia/export` — CSV per modality or "Download All", date-range filter, pseudonymized (patient_code only, never MRN)

- 11 new tables (patients, patient_identifiers, visit_schedule, transfusions, lab, echo, ecg, t2mri, polysomnography, scg, adverse_events)

Closes #163

## Summary
`-e` overrides were merged into a `--state` file's loaded dict with a plain `dict.update()` call, *before* `migrate_legacy_state` ran. When the `--state` file was itself a namespaced snapshot (e.g. a prior `--out`), it already had an `input` key, so the lift short-circuited and the fresh `-e` key stayed stranded at the root — unreachable via `{{input.<key>}}`. Extracted a `_apply_inline_overrides()` helper used at both CLI merge sites (`run_cmd`, `run_library_cmd`): if the loaded `--state` file already has an `input` dict, `-e` values are merged directly into it (still winning over any existing `input.<key>`); otherwise they fall through to the root as before, where the usual lift-on-hydrate wraps everything together.

author: kjinkinsight-ctrl
body:
`concept` was a bare `general-lore` child with **no fields at all** — an idea a whole plot argues about, recorded with a title, a summary and a blank page.

## The fields are built around disagreement, not definition

An idea nobody contests generates no story. `objections` — the strongest case against, the one a reader would make — is the field an author is most likely to skip and most likely to need. An idea with no answer to it reads as a strawman.

| section | fields |
|---|---|
| The claim | what it holds, what follows, what it asks of you |
| Contested | objections, opposed to, held by, standing |
| Origin | where it came from, and who first argued it |

## Claiming `concept` is the most general claim any system has made

So the file argues for it rather than assuming it. Four base types have been declined across the programme — `item`, `location`, `travel-route`, `world` — each because **other types inherit it and services resolve membership through it**.

`concept` is neither. It is a leaf: nothing descends from it, nothing resolves through it. The generic that actually means *"somewhere to write an idea down"* is `general-lore`, and that stays unclaimed and always offered.

Both halves are asserted — and a mutation that claims `general-lore` instead **fails three tests**. A fifth entry now joins the declined-base-type guard.

## No type was invented to pad it

| declined | because |
|---|---|
| `school-of-thought` | a body of people; `institution` and `faction` model that |
| `tenet` | bounded — a philosophy has a handful, so it is a field |
| `argument` | `objections` and `implications` are fields on the concept |
| `ideology` | a concept with adherents; the edges carry the adherents |

A test asserts each is still absent, so if one becomes a real type, whoever adds it inherits the argument.

## `standing` is free text, deliberately

`shortText`, not `singleChoice` — the same reasoning as `deity.status`. The field system has no custom-value support, so a fixed list would refuse an author whose idea is in a state nobody anticipated. A mutation making it a fixed list fails.

## Mutation testing

| mutation | caught by |
|---|---|
| claim `general-lore` instead of the leaf | 3 tests |
| shadow inherited `notes` with `objections` | 2 tests |
| make `standing` a fixed option list | 1 test |

## A note on the analyzer count

The baseline on current `main` is **84**, not the 78 this programme has reported since PR 0. Those six arrived with another lane's merges, **not** with this change — verified by stashing and re-running against clean `main`. This PR adds none, and there are still **0 errors**.

- `flutter analyze` — **84 issues / 0 errors** (baseline unchanged)

- `flutter build web --release --no-web-resources-cdn` — succeeds
- `git diff --check` — clean

author: jonhill90
body:
Closes #623.

Completion can now **adopt** a result file that already exists on disk instead of refusing it.

## The bug this fixes

A lane finishes, writes its result to `results/<task>.md`, and dies before the ledger row is updated. The row keeps `status=delivered` with `result_path` NULL. From then on the task cannot be completed by *either* path — both try to write a result and hit the immutability guard:

```
$ cli.py record-completion --lane agent-supervisor:4 --note '...'
  core.py:3289 in _write_result
  ValueError: immutable result conflicts with existing content

$ cli.py reconcile-lane-completions --idle-after 300
  {"errors":[{"error":"immutable result conflicts with existing content",
              "task":"as531-fix620"},
             {"error":"immutable result conflicts with existing content",
              "task":"as531-rev620b"}], ...}
```

Two of this session's worker lanes were stranded that way — idle, undispatchable, each holding real completed work product, and unrecoverable by any existing verb.

## Scope, from the merge base

```
 scripts/supervisor/core.py                        | 44 ++++++++++++---
 tests/supervisor/test_core.py                     | 44 +++++++++++++++
 tests/supervisor/test_reconcile_lane_completions.py | 57 ++++++++++++++++++
 3 files changed, 138 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)
```

## What has NOT been verified

**This PR was recovered from the lane's worktree and pushed on its behalf; it has not been independently reviewed, and I have not confirmed the mutation evidence the brief required.** A reviewer must establish, by running rather than reading:

- The adopt path records `result_sha256` equal to the file's actual hash.
- **A row that already records a hash still refuses different content.** This is the direction the immutability guard exists for; a fix that loses it silently destroys a lane's own output and is worse than the bug.
- Both `record-completion` and `reconcile-lane-completions` are fixed — they share the code and the brief required both.
- The mutation checks were applied, not merely claimed (`#623`'s brief asked for the changed line to be printed before each run).

Note also `#624`: the pre-push guard refuses correctly-dispatched lanes over a path-spelling mismatch, which is why this branch was pushed from the primary checkout rather than by its own lane.

author: im-ian
body:
## Why

After #859 removed the doubled per-write repaint, scrolling Claude Code's REPL still felt sluggish — and only Claude's REPL, not other TUIs. A new perf probe (driving the real Terminal component with a mocked PTY on both Chromium and WebKit) explains both observations: the input half of a scroll tick is healthy everywhere (~0.25ms per wheel event), but WebKit's DOM renderer consumes a Claude-style full-screen truecolor redraw in ~25ms while one wheel notch asks the TUI for up to 8 of them, so frames back up. A vim-like delta stream (3 rows per frame) stays at display cadence on the same pipeline — the choke is per-frame render volume, which only full-repaint TUIs like Claude's Ink renderer produce, and only the wheel-owning TUI path triggers.

## What

Scope the WebGL renderer to the one interaction that needs it. A small controller (`src/lib/terminalWebglBurst.ts`) loads `@xterm/addon-webgl` on the first wheel event aimed at a TUI that owns the wheel, and disposes it back to the DOM renderer after 1.5s of wheel quiet, the moment IME composition renders, or on GL context loss (which disables the feature for that terminal's lifetime instead of retrying every wheel). The DOM renderer remains the resting state because IME composition anchoring, the span-cloning IME tail view, and transparent terminal backgrounds depend on it; a see-through background skips WebGL entirely.

Measured on the WebKit probe (40-frame truecolor full-screen burst, 8ms cadence, realistic 12-color palette): stream consumption 1071ms → 501ms, rAF gap p50 26ms → 17ms (display cadence), p95 31ms → 25ms. Real hardware runs Metal-backed GL rather than headless fallback, so the shipped app should do at least this well.

Known limits: a one-time GL context setup hitch on the first wheel of a burst (the 1.5s quiet window keeps re-activation rare), and WebGL stays off for transparent backgrounds.

author: 1vivy
body:
Hardening series from two field failures. Nothing here changes the exploit, the modes, or the lock-state projection.

## What the two reports actually were

**Hard brick (EDL 9008, no fastboot).** Fresh module install → recovery → BDS menu → `Android` → OrangeFox → format data → reboot → vendor logo, black screen, `QUSB_BULK_CID`, no bootloop, no fastboot text. No EDL pull will ever be available. Nothing in this repository sets an active slot, decrements a retry counter, or marks a slot successful, and selecting `Android` only writes the bounded 1 KiB default record. What fits: the first *system* boot failed, the retries drained, the bootloader swapped slots, and the slot it swapped to carried an ABL that cannot run on that device. Fresh install pairs **only** the active slot, so any first-boot failure escalated from "reflash" to "EDL".

**Chainload → canoe upgrade, recoverable.** Bootloader and recovery fine, system will not boot, reverting the older install boots. Shape: canoe's BDS in `efisp` over a persist tree from another generation. The two halves are written by independent steps with no identity handshake, and every fallback on the boot path is silent.

## Commits

| commit | what |
|---|---|
| `abl-tzmap: add verify…` | `AblDigest` has been carried since the map was introduced and was never compared to anything. New `abl_tzmap verify --sidecar --abl [--allow-zero-digest]`; BDS gains an observability-only digest marker in `SfbLoadTzMap`. |
| `ablrepo: record per-image identity…` | `abl.meta` per product (product/model/soc/abl_version/sha256/bytes, `same_image_as`, informational `codename`). README stops claiming a re-patch check that did not exist. Four dirs (CPH2841, OPD2513, PLR110, PMA120) are recorded as sharing one binary — disclosed as a warning sign, not an endorsement. Every unevidenced field is the literal `unknown`. No image added, removed, or modified. |
| `module: gate the ABL downgrade…` | The real fix. Candidate image is extracted+patched and refused unless the GBL patch succeeds; `abl.meta` must agree with the device; **the pair is re-derived after the downgrade** and the install aborts if the flashed ABL still lacks the vulnerability; staged tzmap is verified against the loader from the ABL on flash. The ABL write gets size-fit, snapshot, hash readback and restore-on-mismatch — it was the only firmware write here without them. A committed install now pairs the inactive slot when that slot is not already vulnerable, warning-only. |
| `canoe-device: stamp the installed generation…` | `.canoe.gen` inside the existing transaction (informational; nothing refuses to boot because of it) and unmanaged boot-root entries moved into `.canoe.foreign/`, reported, never deleted, never overwritten. |
| `canoe-host: verify the tzmap sidecar…` | Build fails on a digest mismatch; stage verifies when the ABL is beside the triplet and skips with one explicit line when it is not — a stage the previous release accepted does not start failing. |
| `docs: name the failure signatures…` | Symptom → cause → recovery for EDL/9008-black-screen and for system-won't-boot-with-working-bootloader, both languages. Uninstall documents the superfastboot relock path for devices where stock fastboot never appears, including why `flashing lock` must precede erasing the chain. |

## Deliberately not done

* No anti-rollback gating. SM8850 has no bootchain ARB fuses and AVB ARB is recoverable by a full fastboot/OTA flash.
* No change to lock-state behaviour and **no change to `BLTools`** — the hooks mutating real state to unlocked is the intended red-screen avoidance, and BL Tools is upstream-inherited, so it needs upstream review, not a patch from here.
* No mode-record changes: Mode 1 ↔ Mode 2 differ only in lock projection on OOS-based firmware and the keys are interchangeable, so there is nothing to migrate and mode selection is already enumerated in the BDS.
* No exit-to-ABL path. Verified separately that `SfbBuildMenu` reserves four slots and appends `Enter Fastboot` unconditionally, so superfastboot is already served in every case.
* No upstream-inherited file touched: nothing under `AndroidToolsPkg`, `FastbootLib`, `PartitionTableUpdate`, or generic EDK2 packages. The only UEFI edit is one DEBUG line in this project's own `SuperFbLaunchPolicy.c`. The shipped `BDS.efi` is not rebuilt, so the byte-identical-BDS invariant holds.

## Verification

Every targeted suite touched by this branch, all green:

```
sh targets/magisk_module/tests/test_flows.sh          rc=0
sh targets/magisk_module/tests/test_webui.sh          rc=0
sh tools/canoe-device/tests/test_canoe_device_install.sh  rc=0  (11 fixtures)
python -m pytest tools/canoe-host/tests -q            rc=0  (43 passed)
cargo test --manifest-path tools/abl-tzmap/Cargo.toml rc=0
cargo test --manifest-path tools/mode2-profile/Cargo.toml rc=0
```

New coverage: staging refused when the GBL warning survives a downgrade; candidate image refused when it does not take the patch; ABL write rolled back and reported on a readback mismatch; sidecar/ABL digest mismatch rolling back the pair; inactive-slot pairing skipped when already vulnerable and warning-only on failure; `.canoe.gen` written/restored/removed across rollback and tree-only runs; foreign file set aside, preserved on collision, rolled back; build/stage verify pass, fail, and skip. `abl.meta` self-consistency was checked against the images on disk for all 13 directories (sha256, bytes, committed `abl.sha256`, `same_image_as` symmetry).

Not verified on hardware — no device in this loop. The module path is exercised only through the flow fixtures.

## Merge ordering caveat

The module now requires `abl.meta` for a repo downgrade, and the cloud fallback fetches it from `main`. The bundled copy inside the module ZIP is tried first, so a build cut from this branch works standalone — but **merge this before shipping a module build**, or the cloud fallback will refuse on `main` until the metadata exists there.

## Summary

Michael asked via Teams to prioritize a real BTA meeting over two President Weekly Block Schedule blocks. The bot said it could only check availability, then got stuck in a confused, self-contradictory UTC/Central timezone loop, and never actually resolved anything — it just kept asking Michael to hand-pick new slots for the displaced blocks. Three distinct root causes, all traced to the live log (`logs/agent.log`) and fixed:

### 1. Misrouted intent (`teams/router.js`)
"Client meeting block" tripped `isCrmActionRequest`'s bare `\bclient\b` token, routing the whole request to `'crm'` — a taskType with zero calendar tools (only `BOOKING_TOOLS`'s availability check). Confirmed in the log: `Tool call: check_michael_availability` → `escalate_to_claude_code`. The escalation feature (#321) worked exactly as designed, but the real gap was upstream routing, not a missing capability.

Added `isCalendarRescheduleRequest`, checked ahead of the CRM classifier — same "narrower signal wins" precedent as the existing email/inbox carve-out in `isReportRequest`.

### 2. Timezone bug (`tools/impl/m365.js`)
`listCalendarEvents` (the exposed `list_calendar_events` tool) was the one calendar-read function missing the `Prefer: outlook.timezone` header every sibling function (`getCalendarViewWithCategories`, `getCalendarEvent`) already sends. Graph returned raw UTC, and the model tried to do UTC→Central arithmetic in its own head across multiple turns, getting it wrong and self-contradictory each time ("16:00 UTC... wait, let me recalculate...").

### 3. No conversational way to trigger the already-built auto-displacement logic
Phase 3's `reconcileRealEventAgainstBlocks` (`block-schedule-reconciler.js`, live since 2026-08-24) already does exactly this — shrink/split/delete overlapping blocks in favor of a real event, any tier, per Michael's confirmed rule. But it was only ever called from the `calendar_change_watch` cron task, never reachable from live chat. The model had no way to run it on demand, so it improvised from raw reads and asked Michael to do the work himself.

Added:
- `findCalendarEventsBySubject` (`m365.js`) — locates a real event by subject substring + local date, deliberately returning bare-UTC times so it's drop-in compatible with the reconciler's existing input contract (same shape as `calendar-watch.js`'s `getCalendarChanges()`).
- `resolveCalendarConflictBySubject` (`block-schedule-reconciler.js`) — finds the event, then runs the existing reconciler against it. Never guesses on 0 or 2+ matches, same convention as `scheduleEstimateVisit`'s client lookup.
- New `resolve_calendar_conflict` agent tool + a `'calendar'` intent branch in `teams/bot.js`.

**Verified read-only against the real calendar**: `findCalendarEventsBySubject({subjectContains: 'BTA', date: '2026-08-27'})` correctly returns exactly one match — "BTA Implementation - Landscaping & Home Services," 11:00 AM–1:00 PM Central, organizer `support@btacademy.com` (matches the existing BTA auto-accept rule) — confirming the whole lookup chain works end-to-end. Did not run the actual mutating reconcile call against production data as part of this PR; that's the test plan below.

## Also fixed
`tools/impl/claude-code-escalation.js` now auto-expires a session's stale pending escalation (>30 min unanswered) before creating a new one. Found three orphaned pending rows from tonight's conversation (unrelated questions Michael never explicitly said yes/no to) that would have piled up into a confusing "you have 3 pending escalations — which one?" prompt on his next unrelated "yes". Cleaned up manually in Supabase; this prevents recurrence.

author: swinney
body:
closes #122 ### Summary The PR stops a reasoning model's chain-of-thought from streaming to the user as the answer, by gating visible emission on the provider's configured `enable_thinking`. - Adds `thinking_gate.py`: two pure functions that decide from provider config alone whether streamed text must be held. - Holds visible text in both `stream()` and `astream()` until a closing think tag ends the model's current reasoning block. - Scopes the gate per reasoning phase, so each model call in a tool-using ReAct loop must close its own block. - Keeps non-thinking and structured-reasoning providers streaming chunk-by-chunk, pinned by guards that passed before the change. - Delivers a held final phase through the `final` event ahead of any stale earlier message, so no answer is dropped. - Leaves runtime validation outstanding in #340; no standing deployment currently enables thinking. ### Confidence Score: 5/5 The PR appears safe to merge, with review round 5 returning no findings on the head commit, all seven CI checks green, and the suite at 3161 passed with 100% patch coverage. Every one of the eleven defects found across five review rounds is fixed and pinned by a test that was red first, on both stream paths; the gate fails closed, so an absent or malformed provider block streams exactly as it does today and cannot raise. The sync/async duplication that made four rounds each surface the same class of defect is recorded as #350 and is additionally non-blocking, as is the runtime descope to #340 — `enable_thinking` is `false` on fasrc-dev, so this code is inert there until thinking is turned on.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/archi/pipelines/agents/utils/thinking_gate.py | Adds `provider_emits_thinking()` and `hold_visible()`, resolving the provider block without regard to case and never raising on a malformed config. | | src/archi/pipelines/agents/base_react.py | Resolves the gate from the provider the model was actually built with, and honors the reasoning-phase boundary at every site in both stream paths. | | tests/unit/test_thinking_gate.py | Covers the exact-`True` rule, case-insensitive provider matching, every absent and non-mapping level, and the hold-and-release predicate. | | tests/unit/test_base_react_streaming_think_leak.py | Drives both stream paths through the leak, the post-tool-call phase, the structured channel, the error exits, and the over-suppression guard. | | tests/unit/test_request_local_pipeline.py | Proves through the real builder that the gate follows a request-local provider override and ignores a same-provider model switch. | | docs/docs/fasrc_archi.md | Documents what turning `enable_thinking` back on now does to streaming, beside the existing section on turning it off. | | openspec/changes/fix-issue-122-streaming-think-leak/specs/agent-streaming-thinking/spec.md | Scopes the requirement to the current reasoning phase and adds scenarios for tool calls, the structured channel, and provider-name case. |

Flowchart

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Streamed delta arrives] --> B{Provider sends a separate reasoning_content field?} B -- Yes --> C[Reasoning stays separate, content emits as before] B -- No --> D[Parse thinking out of the accumulated content] D --> E{Provider config enables thinking?} E -- No --> F[Emit the visible text event] E -- Yes --> G{Has this phase closed its think tag?} G -- Yes --> F G -- No --> H[Hold the text and leave last_visible_content unchanged] H --> I{Does the stream complete normally?} I -- Yes --> J[The final event still carries the whole answer] I -- No --> K[Held text is discarded, error output unchanged] F --> L{A tool call starts the next model call?} L -- Yes --> M[Reset the phase marker so the next block must close its own tag] M --> G ```
--- ### Background Issue #84 and PR #121 sanitized the stored and final answer. The live display still leaked: with `enable_thinking` true a Qwen-style chat template pre-fills the `` opener, so the model begins generating inside its reasoning block and closes it with an orphan tag that has no opener. Until that tag arrives `_parse_thinking_content()` has nothing to strip, so the reasoning is the visible content and reaches the screen as the answer. The July design gated suppression on "thinking content has been produced and no closing tag has been seen". Those conditions are mutually exclusive, so that predicate is a **no-op** — it is false during exactly the window that leaks. The 2026-08-11 nightly run proved it. The operator chose the config-keyed gate on **2026-08-23**, recorded in plan PR #324, and re-confirmed it on 2026-08-24. The discriminator has to come from outside the stream, because before the closing tag reasoning bytes and a plain answer are the same characters in the same order. The gate reads the provider's own `extra_kwargs.extra_body.chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`, and reads it from `self.default_provider` rather than `services.chat_app.default_provider`, so a request-local provider switch tracks it with no extra plumbing. Because a ReAct run makes one model call per tool round and each call gets its own pre-filled opener, the gate is scoped to the **current reasoning phase**: a closing tag from an earlier phase does not release a later one. ### Validation status Unit coverage is **complete**: groups 1–4 and 6 of the merged plan, every test red before green. Runtime validation is **outstanding in #340**. Task group 5 is descoped there deliberately, because neither default surface can prove anything: the PR preview stack runs Ollama, which reports reasoning through the separate `reasoning_content` field and never reaches the leaking branch, and fasrc-dev sets `enable_thinking: false` as this leak's standing workaround. A green run on either stack as configured must not be recorded as validation of this change. ### Review history Two pre-PR adversarial rounds, then three rounds on the open PR. The round-log comments carry the per-finding verdicts. Three corrections are worth surfacing here: - **A pre-PR rebuttal of mine was wrong.** I claimed the recursion wrap-up still sees held text. It does not: `latest_messages` is overwritten on every stream event (`base_react.py:492`) and `all_messages` skips chunks, so the wrap-up prompt sees only the final delta. Nothing in this PR relies on that claim. - **The multi-phase leak was missed pre-PR and caught by both reviewers.** `accumulated_content` is never reset across tool rounds, so the first phase's closing tag held the gate open for every later model call. Fixed, and pinned by a test that was red beforehand. - **One scenario was briefly made worse than the bug.** When a held final phase followed a narrated tool call, the end-of-stream scan returned the narration and the real answer reached the user nowhere at all — where before this PR it at least streamed. Fixed by preferring the held phase; the guard engages only for a thinking-enabled provider whose current phase has no closing tag. - **Round 3's enumeration was scoped too narrowly.** It listed every consumer of `accumulated_content` and claimed the class was closed. Round 4's three findings were all about how the gate's *inputs* are derived — tool-call phase detection and provider resolution — and none of them reads that buffer, so none appeared in the list. Round 4 also disproved the merged design's Decision 3, which says reading `self.default_provider` tracks the provider "with no extra plumbing": it is never set on a pipeline-map construction, and the gate failed open there. **Round 5 came back clean** on the head commit, which is the loop's terminal condition. Round 4's log had said the loop was not converging and asked for a human call before merge; round 5 falsif

author: huang-404-q
body:
## What

`_terminal_status_for_exit` mapped every non-zero worker exit to `failed`, so a run that deliberately ends `blocked` or `incomplete` (round budget exhausted, manager blocked) is relabelled as a crash.

## Why

- The CLI exits non-zero for **every** non-completed run: `return 0 if final_report.get("completion_satisfied") else 1` (`cli.py:1865`). The exit code therefore carries no crash signal once a final report exists.
- `lifecycle.py` defines `blocked`/`incomplete` in `TERMINAL_STATUSES` with the comment "terminal from the supervisor's point of view and **may be retried/resumed**" — a non-crash, resumable outcome.
- The bug shows two symptoms:
  1. A normal max-rounds-exhausted run becomes `status=failed` + a spurious `crash_report.json` (`_persist_failure_report` fires whenever the lifecycle is `failed`).
  2. The same run reconciled through the no-`Popen` path (API restart, where `returncode=0 if report else 1`) reports `incomplete` — i.e. the outcome depends on whether the supervisor process was restarted.

## Change

- Add `RESUMABLE_OUTCOMES = frozenset({"blocked", "incomplete"})` to `lifecycle.py`.
- In `_terminal_status_for_exit`, check the completion-authority rule before the exit code, then on a non-zero exit return the report's status only when it is one of `RESUMABLE_OUTCOMES`; everything else (no report, a crash report's `failed`/`cancelled`, a success claim from a dead process) stays `failed`.

The set is deliberately only the two resumable outcomes, not all of `TERMINAL_STATUSES`: crash reports always carry `failed`/`cancelled`, and a non-zero exit with a `completed` report is still a failure — the existing hardening test `test_nonzero_worker_exit_is_failed_and_persists_crash_report` (which writes a forged authorised report and expects `failed`) passes unchanged.

## How I checked

- New `tests/supervisor/test_terminal_status.py`: 8 mapping tests + 2 end-to-end tests through `RunSupervisor.status()` (asserts no spurious `crash_report.json` for a real `incomplete` report, and `failed` + crash report when none exists).
- Red-light: with the fix reverted, exactly the 3 new outcome-preservation tests fail and the 7 semantic-preservation tests pass.
- Full suite: 415 passed, 1 skipped. No existing test modified.

## Summary
The `runQuiz()` 09:00-21:00 window (V96.24) was a hard `alert()`-and-block with no way around it. This adds a request/approve flow:

- **Intern**: blocked outside the window → `confirm()` offers to submit a request instead of a dead-end alert. `requestOutOfHours()` writes `outOfHoursRequested: true` on the quiz_attempts doc (merge-safe, doesn't disturb an in-progress attempt).
- **Admin**: new listener for `outOfHoursRequested == true`, merged into the existing Pending Quizzes table/badge. **Allow Once** sets `outOfHoursApproved: true`; **Deny** just clears the request flag. Neither touches `status` or deletes the doc.
- **Scope**: approval is single-attempt, single-use — the flag is consumed (`FieldValue.delete()`) the moment the quiz actually starts, so a later attempt needs a fresh request. This matches the explicit ask: *"เฉพาะ quiz นั้นใบเดียว ครั้งนั้นครั้งเดียว"*.

## Why two Firestore listeners instead of one query
Admin's existing pending query is `status in ["pending","requesting"]`. The SDK here is firebase-firestore-compat v8.10.1, which has no `Filter.or()`, so out-of-hours requests use a second `where("outOfHoursRequested","==",true)` listener, merged client-side via `renderCombinedPending()` into the same table/badge.

## No rules/deploy changes needed
`quiz_attempts` already allows `create, update, read` for any signed-in user — no `firestore.rules` change, no manual rules deploy.

- Verified both files' inline `<script>` blocks still parse (Node `new Function()` check); confirmed the 2 pre-existing parse "errors" (a TS-typed snippet + a `<script type="module">` block) are unrelated and pre-date this change.

Closes #201

## Summary
Fixes critical security vulnerabilities in the Timelock governance contract: enforces grace period expiration, validates eta on queue, and restricts delay changes to self-calls only.

### Changes
- **Grace Period Enforcement**: `executeTransaction` now reverts with "Timelock: tx stale" if `block.timestamp > eta + GRACE_PERIOD` (14 days)
- **Eta Validation**: `queueTransaction` requires `eta >= block.timestamp + delay`, preventing immediate execution bypass
- **Access Control on setDelay**: Only the Timelock contract itself (`msg.sender == address(this)`) can change the delay, forcing governance through the timelock process
- **Minimum Delay**: Added `MINIMUM_DELAY = 1 hours` constant; constructor and `setDelay` reject values below it
- **cancelTransaction**: Already existed with proper `onlyAdmin` modifier — verified correct behavior

### Security Fixes
- Prevents queued transactions from being executable forever after delay expires
- Blocks admin from bypassing timelock by queuing with past eta
- Prevents unauthorized delay reduction that would defeat governance protection
- Ensures delay cannot be set to zero

### SOLID / Object Calisthenics
- Single Responsibility: Each function handles one governance operation
- Open/Closed: Constants define policy without modifying logic
- No Static Mutable State: All state flows through contract storage
- Encapsulated Access Control: `onlyAdmin` and self-call checks are declarative modifiers

body:
Two follow-ups that #1182 and #1183 deliberately deferred, now that both are merged and migration 394 is applied in prod.

## 1. One classifier, not two

`src/lib/calling/call-transport.ts` (#1183) and `src/lib/calls/call-kind.ts` (#1182) were written in the same session by different PRs and said the same thing. Folded into `call-kind.ts`; the three UI imports are repointed and the duplicate module and its tests are deleted.

**The two defaults stay different, on purpose, and the code now says why.** They disagree on exactly one input class — unknown / `NULL` / `'manual'` — because the cost of being wrong is opposite:

| predicate | unknown `call_type` → | why |
|---|---|---|
| `classifyCall()` | `browser` | an unrecognised row must never **claim** activation |
| `isBrowserCallType()` | phone | an unrecognised row must never be **labelled** a browser test |

A rep's manually-logged call (`call_type = 'manual'`) badged "WebRTC" is a visible lie about work they did on a real phone. Collapsing the display helper into `classifyCall()` — the obvious "simplification" — would flip every legacy and manual row's badge, so there is a regression test asserting the divergence.

## 2. Re-key the no-first-call nudge to the honest columns

`runNoFirstCall` in `/api/cron/reengagement` was gated on `first_real_call_at` (migration 391), with a comment saying to re-key once 394 landed. It has landed, so it is re-keyed to `first_inbound_pstn_call_at IS NULL AND first_outbound_pstn_call_at IS NULL`.

391's predicate is `from_number IS NOT NULL`, and **1,567 of 1,590 in-browser outbound rows carry a from_number** (both demo routes stamp one), so it could exclude a browser-only org from the one nudge aimed at exactly that org. It is also direction-blind.

Both directions gate the nudge: inbound is what a trial org can actually reach on day 1 (the trial number is provisioned at signup), so an org that has taken an inbound PSTN call has heard the product work and should not get a "you haven't called yet" email. `first_real_call_at` stays in the SELECT projection — nothing reads it — so an old-vs-new cohort diff stays trivial while this is watched.

author: ankitgoenk
body:
## What changed

Decision infrastructure only. **No `HOOK_*` detector** — the size result constrains what the first native detector can afford to cost, so the number comes first.

Two commits:

1. **`99d6398`** — corrects the `APP_NATIVE_LIB_MISMATCH` false-positive analysis and records the phase 3b prerequisites.
2. **`ce5ab27`** — a CI job that measures three native configurations, plus the variant-rewriting tool it uses.

## The measurement

arm64-v8a, release, stripped:

| | Configuration | Containment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | `c++_static`, throws `std::runtime_error` | as shipped — 219 KB |
| B | `c++_static`, `catch (...)` kept, nothing thrown from the STL | full |
| C | `STL=none`, `-fno-exceptions`, status codes only | none |

The two deltas are the point:

- **A → B** is the cost of the STL machinery `<stdexcept>` pulls in — `std::string`, RTTI, libc++.
- **B → C** is the cost of unwinding support itself.

If B lands near C, B is the obvious choice: full containment at most of C's saving. If B lands near A, there's a genuine architectural decision to make rather than an easy optimisation. I have a hypothesis about which, and have deliberately not written it into the plan — the point of the experiment is to replace a guess with a number.

Variants are **generated copies**; production sources are untouched until the data says which way to go.

## The job is also a constraint, not just a benchmark

It fails if the native code stops building under `-fno-exceptions`. Without that, someone later adds a `throw std::runtime_error(...)` and silently removes option C before anyone has chosen it. The measurement job turns "we could still go no-exceptions" from an assumption into something CI enforces.

## Correcting a claim I got wrong

The `APP_NATIVE_LIB_MISMATCH` catalog row said *"FP: none known for the token check itself; it compares two values the build controls."* That was overconfident.

A mismatch fires whenever a host resolves a **stale or skewed `integrity-native` against a newer `integrity-core`** — also on enterprise repackaging, also on a stale incremental build. In the field, dependency hygiene is a far likelier cause than an attacker. The row now says so, and phase 3b gains a concrete task: **report the expected and actual tokens**, which are version strings rather than secrets and are readable from the `.so` anyway. Without them, a version skew is indistinguishable from an attack.

## Detector PRs only

n/a — no detector. No `SignalId` behaviour changes; the catalog edit is to an existing row's risk analysis, which the evidence-chain gate still validates.

## Checks

- [x] All three variants compile-checked on the host toolchain under `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` (C under `-fno-exceptions`) before committing, so the job should return three numbers rather than a build failure
- [x] `bash -n` and an AST parse on the two new scripts
- [x] Evidence-chain gate passes — 13 implemented signals
- [ ] NDK specifics of the measurement — CI is the first real run, as ever

## What the numbers unblock

```
measurement → native runtime decision → first HOOK threat hypothesis
→ clean fixture → positive fixture → known bypass → implement
```

The known bypass gets defined **before** implementation. A detector tested only against the case it was written to catch measures nothing except that the author was consistent with themselves.

Bounds the `cross_family` skill-judge phase's per-call timeout at an evidence-based p90 derived from real `skill_judge_perf` latency samples in `runs/ledger.jsonl`, instead of the fixed 90s constant chosen by hand in issue #2076. Below a 50-genuine-sample threshold the bound stays dormant and today's fixed default is unchanged. Two issues were found and fixed mid-delivery (a warrant-hunt bypass and an operator-flagged unbounded-scan cost) — see below. Closes #2274.

## Summary
- Derives the `skill_judge` per-call timeout from the real `skill_judge_perf` wall_s distribution in `runs/ledger.jsonl` (p90), gated at >=50 genuine samples — below that, the fixed 90s default (issue #2076) is unchanged (empty state).
- No new fail-open machinery: a timeout already routed through `_cross_family_skill_matches_with_consult()`'s existing `except Exception` → BM25 top-k fallback (issue #2040); this only supplies an evidence-based value instead of a hand-picked constant.
- Before-landing `warrant-hunter` dispatch (stance 0) found the first cut of the "genuine sample" filter (`duration_ms is not None` alone) was bypassable by a mocked `subprocess.run` faking `duration_ms` while `wall_s` stayed ~0 — 50+ such entries would have collapsed the cutoff (and the timeout) to ~0s, making every real call fail open. Fixed by also requiring `wall_s >= 1.0s`, with a regression test reproducing the exact PoC.
- An operator-frozen constraint posted on the issue mid-session (no added per-spawn overhead/steady-state load, systemic across installs, no new conflict surfaces) flagged that the filter's full-ledger scan would grow unboundedly with the append-only ledger's lifetime size. Fixed with a bounded 512KiB tail-read (measured ~270x faster at 13MB, and flat regardless of total ledger size), with its own regression test.

Full distribution, derivation, both findings/fixes, and live executed evidence (including a real non-mocked `sleep 5`-under-a-real-timeout fail-open demonstration and the measured before/after read-cost numbers) are in `docs/issue-2274/reports/performance-engineering.md`.

Closes #2274

author: jlengelbrecht
body: Review findings from the promotion PR (#48), which reviews the whole accumulated diff rather than any single change and turned up things the per-change reviews did not. Fixes land here so #48 picks them up from develop; the promotion PR itself needs no edit. ## What changed **A history record answering outside its requested window is now refused by both drivers.** The backfill cursor advances to the highest sequence number a batch hands over and only ever moves forward, so one record decoding to a bogus sequence parks it above anything the pump will ever hold and ends history collection permanently. The orchestrator's span check does not cover that case. It compares how many sequences a batch would carry the cursor over against how many records it brought, which catches a hole in an answer and a garbage index arriving alongside real records. A batch that is nothing but a garbage index spans zero sequences and satisfies the arithmetic, and there is no bound to apply at that layer, because a legitimate leading gap looks identical from there. Only the drivers know the window they asked for. Tandem already checked this. Medtronic did not: `HistoryReader` verified that every frame decoded and that the RACP terminal agreed with what streamed, neither of which says anything about the sequence a cleanly-decoded record claims. It now fails the page, leaving the cursors put so the window is re-read. The orchestrator comment claimed the span check caught both shapes; it now says which layer owns which. **Tandem's empty-range guard compared `lastSeq` against `firstSeq` while the scan starts at the clamped `windowStart`.** A pump reporting `firstSeq = lastSeq = 0` passed it, requested no window at all, and still proposed a scan position, which the caller then promoted on the strength of an empty answer. If the scan had been further along, that rewound it. The cost was re-fetching, not lost records. **Downgrade warning in the install guide.** Schema 14 stops the app wiping its own database on a downgrade, but that only binds builds shipping this code. Every earlier build runs its own destructive builder, so installing an older release after this one erases local pump history, alerts, queued uploads and the raw records kept for re-derivation, with no prompt and no way back. Nothing in the app can say so, because the wipe happens inside the older build. Carries a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer so the release notes carry the warning too. The battery-optimization note read as troubleshooting for frequent disconnects. The exemption is what decides whether Android restarts monitoring at all after a reboot or a disconnect, which is what this release's work is about. **Test and comment corrections.** The wear lock-contention test asserted that a watch message could not mutate the work counter while a start command held the lock, but nothing established that the watch-message thread had reached the contended call, so it would have passed with the lock removed. The `join(timeout)` calls had the same gap in reverse. And `BackgroundStartEligibility`'s comment promised that a visible process qualifies while the check accepts `IMPORTANCE_FOREGROUND_SERVICE` or better; the code is right and the comment was not. ## Findings not acted on Three of the seven were refuted rather than fixed, with reasoning in the review threads: the claim that `fallbackToDestructiveMigrationFrom(dropAllTables = true, ...)` cannot compile (the lockfile pins Room 2.7.0 on every compile and runtime classpath), the claim that backfill uploads can be lost (the loss predates the atomic-commit change and is now recorded rather than silent, with the healing pass tracked separately), and a session-ordering race in `PollLoopHealth` that the orchestrator's cancel-before-launch under one lock makes unreachable. ## Verification `testDebugUnitTest`, `lintDebug`, `assembleDebug`, and `:app:connectedDebugAndroidTest` on emulator-5554 (89 tests). Both new driver tests were confirmed to fail with their guard reverted. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved Medtronic history synchronization by rejecting records outside the requested range. * Fixed Tandem history scans for ranges without usable records, preventing unnecessary scans and incorrect progress updates. * Improved reliability when monitoring and wearable communication operations run concurrently. * **Documentation** * Clarified rollback risks, including database deletion and recovery steps. * Expanded battery-optimization guidance and Android 15 background-operation limitations. * Documented the “Monitoring not running” notification and troubleshooting steps.

body:
## What this PR does / why we need it?

Adapt upstream [#13142](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/13142) decode index TP block-sharding to the A5 branch with a CP switch and two optimization stages:

### Changes

1. **CP switch (Baseline, 3 collectives)**: Add `VLLM_ASCEND_MINIMAX_M3_INDEXER_CP` env switch. When ON, shard the Index-K sequence-block range across the CP group (`tp_size // indexer_num_kv_heads`; for M3 `indexer_num_kv_heads=1` → CP group = full TP group), compute local top-k + scores, AllGather candidates and merge global top-k.

2. **方案 A (2 collectives)**: Pack score (FP32) and index (INT32) into one FP32 tensor via bitcast (not numeric conversion), replacing two separate candidate AllGathers with one.

3. **方案 B (1 collective)**: Replicate full Index-Q projection weights on every rank so each rank projects all index-Q heads directly, deleting the per-layer `idx_q AllGather`. Use `logical_rank = cp_rank // num_index_head_replicas` for head selection in replica scenarios.

### Triton kernel changes (`msa_m3_triton.py`)
- Add `block_offset` / `global_seq_lens` / `return_scores` to `minimax_m3_index_decode` for sharded block scoring.
- Update `_decode_qk_score_kernel` and `_index_topk_postprocess_kernel` to use global block ids for init/local priority and correct masking.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

New env var `VLLM_ASCEND_MINIMAX_M3_INDEXER_CP` (default 0 = disabled). When enabled, requires TP > 1 and pure-decode batches.

## How was this patch tested?

- [ ] TP1/CP1: baseline single-rank path
- [ ] TP4/CP4: pure decode, compare topk vs single-rank
- [ ] TP8/CP8: pure decode, index-head replica
- [ ] Mixed prefill+decode: CP path not taken
- [ ] GPQA / accuracy regression

## Per-layer collectives summary

| Version | idx_q AllGather | candidate AllGather | Total |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Baseline | 1 | 2 (scores + indices) | 3 |
| 方案 A | 1 | 1 (packed) | 2 |
| 方案 B | 0 (replicated weights) | 1 (packed) | 1 |

- vLLM version: v0.26.0
- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/d02df748bf9efd99022f1a062597dc3cb3808485

## What

Bounce delivery to builder panes must always end in a SUBMIT. The inherited-red **ci-repair** bounce (`_handle_ci_repair`) was the one call site that didn't: it delivered its mechanical base-refresh re-task via a raw `herdr pane run` and never pressed Enter. The fix prompt landed in the agent's input buffer and sat there un-submitted — the builder stayed idle on a full buffer while the rail journaled the bounce as delivered, the wake-proof rail then saw no activity and escalated, and the escalation ALSO pasted-not-submitted.

Observed in production 2026-08-24/25: the `main-red-workers-cli` builder (pane w29:p170) wedged on unsubmitted ci-fastbounce findings; reviewer panes were found with unsubmitted text.

## Fix

Route both delivery attempts in the ci-repair bounce through the `herd_driver_send_text` seam (`herdr pane run` + an explicit `herdr pane send-keys Enter`) — the exact submitting wake path every sibling bounce already uses (review refix, ci-fastbounce, stale-detect, healthcheck) and that the live-port twin `LiveActuator._send_wake` already implements. Submitting was always the intent, so **the fix is unconditional and minimal — no new lever**.

Audited every delivery call site (`grep -n 'send-text'` + `herdr pane run` across `agent-watch.sh` / `driver.sh` / `live_runtime.py`): refix bounce, ci-fastbounce, needs-you routing, scribe pointer delivery, review placement, wedge/finish-stall wakes, and the Python `_send_wake` all already submit through the seam. `herdr pane run` has no `--submit`/`--enter` flag, so the explicit `send-keys Enter` is the mechanism (unchanged from HERD-186). The only other raw `herdr pane run` (`herd_driver_agent_resume_deliver`) is a `cd … && <cmd>` shell relaunch into an ENDED session, not a live-TUI findings delivery — intentionally left as-is.

- `tests/test-ci-repair-bounce-submit.sh` — fake-pane harness that models the input buffer (a `pane run` fills it, `send-keys Enter` empties it) and drives the REAL `_handle_ci_repair` live-builder bounce, asserting the buffer ends EMPTY (submitted, not a pending paste) on both the initial delivery and its one re-send. Verified to FAIL against the pre-fix raw `herdr pane run`.
- `tests/test_live_runtime.py::SendWakeSubmitTests` — pins the live-port twin `LiveActuator._send_wake`: the paste is followed by a `send-keys … Enter` on the same pane; a submit is never omitted.

Implements schema v4 — the reviewed two-form manifest grammar with shorthand
expansion, automatic sub-workspace composition, and converging init.

## Final grammar

```jsonc
{
  "schemaVersion": 4,
  "host": "github.com",        // optional; default github.com; hostname only
  "owner": "acme",             // optional default owner
  "repositories": [
    "memsdk",                          // expands + auto-composes
    "other-org/fork",                  // inline owner overrides top-level
    { "name": "inner", "owner": "acme" }, // object shorthand: composes like strings
    { "name": "elsewhere",

}
```

body:
Four modern CLI tools, each into the category it belongs to rather than a new one.

| Page | Category | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| ast-grep | Files & Search, after jq | 3060 |
| hyperfine | Terminal & Shell, after zoxide | 2060 |
| hunk | Git & Collaboration, after delta | 6060 |
| AutoCLI | Network & APIs, after tunnelling | 7050 |

`pre-commit` moves from 6050 to 6070 so hunk sits before the page that closes its category.

## What each page covers

**ast-grep** leads with why text search is the wrong unit for code — a regex misses the call split over three lines and matches the one inside a string — then the three pieces of pattern syntax (`$VAR`, `$$$ARGS`, literal code), the `--interactive` rewrite, and YAML rules as a project-specific linter. Ends with where it stops: it understands syntax, not types or scope.

**hyperfine** covers the flags that make a benchmark honest, `--warmup` and per-run `--prepare` especially, parameter sweeps with `-L`, and how to read a result — compare the deviation, change one thing, benchmark what users wait for.

**hunk** is the review-first TUI from hunk.dev: `hunk diff --watch` while an agent works, and `core.pager "hunk pager"` so the better view arrives without a new command to remember.

**AutoCLI** is the one-command path to structured data from Hacker News, Reddit and others, piped into jq the way the rest of the site expects.

## Two descriptions narrowed to what the tool actually does

- Several unrelated projects ship a CLI called `hunk`. This is the review-first TUI, and it **reviews rather than stages** — there is no stage-this-hunk key. The page says so and points at lazygit and `git add -p` for staging, and at delta for the overlapping pager case, since you don't need both.
- AutoCLI reads sites rather than contracts, so it breaks when a page changes. The page recommends the official Hacker News and Reddit APIs for anything that must not fail, notes that terms of service and rate limits are the caller's responsibility, and flags that its browser mode drives your own logged-in session through a Chrome extension.

## Verification

Built locally with Hugo Extended 0.161.1 (the version CI pins): 103 pages, no errors. Weights are unique across the site and every internal link resolves. Counts in the overview, landing page, and README move to 71 pages.

author: ibrahimweng
body:
A round cap is drawn by pulling the spine back by as far as the cap will reach, so the far side of the cap lands on the line the letter was meant to stop on. How far it reaches is half the pen — and half the pen at the Black is wider than some of the runs it is put on the end of. Pulled back that far, the run has no length left at all.

**A run of no length is not a shorter run.** Its two ends are the same point, so `stitch` welds them into a single node and the letter comes back with fewer nodes than the same letter at a lighter weight. That is a letter that cannot ride the axis.

The Display bracket is where it showed. Its arms are `arch * 0.52`, which *grows* with the pen:

| | 100 | 400 | 700 | 900 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| arm asked for | 133 | 141 | 148 | 153 |
| arm after the cap | 112 | 53 | **0** | **0** |
| nodes in the letter | 18 | 18 | **10** | **10** |

So the pull-back is now held below what the run can spare — which is what `leaning`, ten lines above it, already does for itself (`if (slide > run * 0.8) return 0`), at the same four fifths and against the same measurement. Where the bound bites the cap reaches past its line, which is a smaller wrong than an arm that is not there. A bracket whose arms have gone is not a bracket.

## What it costs and what it buys

**Across the sixteen faces, 27 letter-face pairs left standing → 21, and no face is worse.** The Display goes 20 → 14, and the six it loses are exactly the six whose corners vanished at heavy weight: `bracketleft`, `bracketright`, `logicalnot`, `б`, `Ω`, `Ώ`.

Fifteen of sixteen faces are **identical at the drawn weight, node for node**. The Display moves on 10 glyphs of 452 with its node count unchanged, and both worth looking at are better for it:

- the **`G`** loses a small rectangular nub that was jutting into its aperture
- the **`copyright`**'s inner `C` opens from a closed blob into a letter with an aperture

The collapsed run was making artefacts at the drawn weight too. It was only on the axis that it was fatal.

## Why this is not a fifth attempt at the corners

Four attempts are already written into `kinksOf` with what each cost, all aimed at the corners. The corners were measured first this time, and they are not it: **of the Display's twenty, fourteen resolve every corner they have the same way at all four weights.**

That measurement had to be taken with the bowl book open and read back. On a bare drawing a bowl's piece list begins wherever that weight's arithmetic puts it, so the lists come out rotated against each other — asked without a book it reports six letters whose spine changes shape with the pen, and none of them do. `scripts/bones.ts` says so at the top of the file.

## One thing tried and thrown away

If a line of no length were never welded shut, the count would not depend on whether there was anything to weld. But the swallowed branch of a corner sets `before.to = before.from`, so lines of no length are how corners get resolved all over the font — refusing to weld them took the sixteen faces from 27 standing to **1,489**, the Sans alone from 0 to 159. The discrimination has to be upstream of the sweep, where a run is either given a length or not.

## Tests

Two, both checked by taking the fix out again and watching them go red:

- the Display bracket has one node count across the axis rather than two
- no straight run on any face at any weight is taken down to nothing

A first version of the first one scaled the pen on its own instead of weighting the family, and **passed with the fault still in** — the arms only vanish once every measurement the arch is built from has moved. A test that reproduces most of the setup reproduces none of the bug.

## Instruments

`scripts/tally.ts` — every face, how many letters it leaves standing, one page. This is the number everything here was measured against.
`scripts/drawnbytes.ts` — fingerprints the outlines at the drawn weight, taken from the contours rather than the file, because the file carries a timestamp and hashes differently every run.
`scripts/moved.ts` — how far the drawn weight moved, and on which glyphs.

1,029 unit tests and 92 browser tests pass; typecheck clean. Run locally — GitHub Actions is still failing account-wide before any job is assigned a runner, red on `main` too and unrelated to this diff.

body:
PR C of #130. Adds `RegularityLemmata/Finite/BinaryTreeRamsey.lean` and the
`RegularityLemmata/FiniteRamsey.lean` facade.

**Replaces #136**, whose base branch is the pre-squash PR B branch and so diverges from `main`.
This branch is built from fresh `origin/main` and carries only PR C's two commits, cherry-picked
cleanly; the review history is on #136.

Based directly on `main` — nothing to sequence. This completes the #130 implementation; the
v0.5.0 release is the remaining step.

## The theorem

```lean
theorem binaryTreeRamsey_two (a b : ℕ) (colour : BinaryTreeTwoColouring (a + b + 1)) :
    (∃ e : InternalEmbedding (a + 1) (a + b + 1), ∀ x, colour (e x) = 0) ∨
    (∃ e : InternalEmbedding (b + 1) (a + b + 1), ∀ x, colour (e x) = 1)
```

Successor heights throughout, no truncated subtraction anywhere in the statement.

## The recursion is indexed by the host height, not by `a + b`

This is the one structural decision worth review. A private auxiliary takes the host height `n`
as its induction variable and carries `a + b = n` as an ordinary hypothesis:

```lean
private theorem ramsey_aux : ∀ (n a b : ℕ), a + b = n →
    ∀ colour : BinaryTreeTwoColouring (n + 1), …
```

The reason is concrete. `Nat` addition recurses on its **second** argument, so `a + (b+1)` is
definitionally `(a+b)+1` but `(a+1) + b` is stuck. The induction needs recursive calls at both
`(a-1, b)` and `(a, b-1)`, so inducting on `a + b` directly would leave one of the two branches
needing a height cast on the colouring and another on the resulting embedding. With the height as
its own variable the branches of a height-`n+1` tree are height `n` definitionally, and every
relation among `a`, `b`, and the height becomes a `Nat` equation that `omega` discharges. No
transport appears anywhere.

## Where the embedding conventions are used

At a root of colour `0`, the `(a-1, b)` case runs in each branch. If either returns the colour-`1`
alternative, that answers the whole tree. Otherwise both return colour-`0` subtrees of height `a`,
found at **unknown depth** inside the branches, and `fork` attaches them under the root. The
assembled embedding therefore sends its root below the host root and turns source edges into long
host paths. Root preservation or depth preservation would make this step impossible — which is
what the falsification tests in #134 pin.

## A consequence worth flagging, and it is worse than a `simp`

`binaryTreeRamsey_two 0 b` produces a colouring type of `0 + b + 1`, not `b + 1`, and those are
**not** definitionally equal for variable `b` — `Nat` addition recurses on its second argument.

`simp [Nat.zero_add]` does **not** close this gap. The height occurs in the type of the bound
colouring, and the body depends on that binder, so rewriting it would require transporting the
body; `simp` will not build that cast and reports no progress. I verified this against both
`Nat.zero_add` and `zero_add`.

What a consumer must actually do is restrict the colouring along the height inequality on the
way in and rebuild the embedding on the way out — both `omega` on word lengths plus proof
irrelevance, with the branch law passing through untouched. The `a = 0` test is now written in
consumer shape (`colour : BinaryTreeTwoColouring (b + 1)`) and performs exactly that conversion,
so the real cost is pinned in the source rather than discovered downstream. No specialization is
added.

## The whole-tree form

`binaryTreeRamsey_two_proper` gives the same dichotomy with `ProperEmbedding`, so what is
exhibited is a copy of the full tree of the stated height and not only of its interior. This is
beyond the letter of the #130 plan for PR C; I added it because "contains a colour-`0` embedded
tree of height `a + 1`" reads as a claim about a tree, leaves included, and because it is the
only consumer of `extendProper` in the campaign — without it PR B has no caller. It is three
lines and introduces no new concept. Say the word if you would rather it were dropped.

## Facade

`RegularityLemmata.FiniteRamsey` re-exports `MulticolorRamsey` together with the four binary-tree
modules, and the **root now imports that facade** instead of listing the Ramsey modules
individually, as specified. The root docstring is updated from three curated facades to four.

The docstring states that the facade collects the library's independent finite Ramsey APIs, and
that neither half is built from the other — the pair colouring lives on an unstructured vertex
set, the tree colouring on the interior of a binary tree.

## Provenance

`PROVENANCE.md` now carries the Lemma 16 theorem identification and the `p = a+1`, `q = b+1`
substitution, alongside the embedding-semantics attribution added in PR A and the
proper-extension sentence added in PR B. It also states explicitly that this is a precise upper theorem with
no optimality claim, since no lower-bound colouring is formalized. The same wording appears in
the module docstring; the earlier "exact" phrasing has been removed from both.

## Tests
